name: ICP and account research
goal: Decide who is worth contacting and prepare a short, sourced brief for each account before any message is written.
when: Before every campaign, and whenever replies suggest you are targeting the wrong people.
inputs: 5 to 10 of your best past customers (anonymised is fine)
3 to 5 customers that churned or never bought

steps.do: Paste the customer descriptions and run the ICP prompt. Review the criteria, disqualifiers and signals it proposes.
Edit the ICP to match what you actually know. Remove any criterion you cannot check from public information.
Turn the criteria into a saved search (industry, company size, role, geography). Save 25 accounts.
Cross-check the same filters in Apollo and compare the lists. Export only the fields you need.
For each account, paste only public information you collected and run the account-brief prompt.
Record account, source URL, signal, date checked and your fit score (1 to 5).

prompt:
You are helping me define an ideal customer profile (ICP) for B2B outreach.

My offer: [two sentences]

Best customers (anonymised):
[paste 5-10 descriptions: industry, size, role of buyer, why they bought]

Customers that churned or never bought:
[paste 3-5 descriptions]

Tasks:
1. Propose an ICP: firmographics, buyer roles, trigger events, and 3 qualifying questions.
2. List disqualifiers.
3. List signals I can check from PUBLIC information only (name each place to check).
4. Flag any criterion that is only a guess from this small sample.
Do not invent facts about any company.
review: You approve the final ICP and score every account yourself. Claude does not decide who gets contacted.
stop: Fewer than half of your sample accounts fit the ICP when you check by hand
You cannot find a public source for a signal: drop that signal
metrics: % of accounts you rate 4 or 5 on fit
% of briefs with a factual error found on review
risks: A small sample producing a misleading ICP
Using data you were not entitled to collect
Treating a signal as proof of intent

runs.sample: 10 accounts: IT and software services firms in India (6 from one Apollo company search, 4 from public directories)
runs.setup: Claude drafted account briefs from public web pages. One Apollo search used 1 credit. Each account scored on a 5-point rubric: located in India, size 50 to 250 evidenced, offers software/mobile/AI services, verified on an official source, dated public signal found. Scored by Claude; no human review yet.
runs.result: Mean fit score 3.35 of 5. 5 of 10 scored 4. 1 of 10 had a dated public signal. Official site readable for 5 of 10. 3 of 10 Apollo results were not services firms (30%). Spot-check: 17 of 17 sampled claims matched the source (4 official sites).
runs.notes: Apollo's employee band conflicted with one official site (400+ staff). Scores measure criteria match and research confidence, not likelihood to buy. The ICP (prospect, partner or competitor) was unresolved. Time saved was not measured. Small sample: directional only.

name: Signal-based first touch
goal: Write a short first message that references one real, public signal and makes a low-pressure ask.
when: After an account brief exists with a dated, sourced signal.
inputs: One public signal with source URL and date
Your sender profile (role, why you are relevant)

steps.do: Run the first-touch prompt with the brief and one signal. Ask for two variants.
Fact-check every claim against the source. Delete anything you cannot source.
Read it aloud. If it sounds like a template, rewrite the first line yourself.
Send manually or schedule in your sending tool with your own opt-out line.
Log send date, variant, signal used and whether you edited the draft.

prompt:
Write two first-touch messages (max 90 words each) to [role] at [company].

Public signal: [signal] (source: [URL], date: [date])
My offer, one sentence: [offer]
Why I am relevant: [one sentence]

Rules:
- Mention the signal once, factually. No flattery.
- Explain the possible link to my offer in one sentence, and say it is a guess.
- End with a low-pressure question they can answer in a few words.
- No jargon, no exclamation marks, no fake urgency.
- Do not state anything about the company that is not in the signal above.
Then list every factual claim you made so I can verify it.
review: A person reads and sends every message. Nothing is auto-sent. Remove any claim without a source.
stop: The message needs more than one personal detail to feel relevant: choose another account
The recipient has opted out or asked not to be contacted
risks: Sending at a volume that harms sender reputation

name: Follow-up sequence with stop rules
goal: Follow up politely with something useful each time, and stop at clear limits.
when: For anyone who has not replied to the first message after a few days.
inputs: One genuinely useful asset or insight for each follow-up

steps.do: Run the follow-up prompt to draft three short follow-ups that each add something new.
Check each follow-up adds value you can actually deliver. Cut any that only 'bump' the thread.
Schedule with a gap of several days between touches. Exclude anyone who replied or opted out.
Mark the sequence status. After the last touch, move the contact to 'closed, no response' for a cooling-off period.

prompt:
Here is my first message and the contact's role:
[paste]

Draft three follow-ups, each under 70 words:
1. Adds one short, specific insight relevant to their role.
2. Shares a small, useful resource or example (describe it; I will attach it).
3. A polite closing note that makes it easy to say 'not now' and stops there.

Rules: no guilt-tripping, no 'just checking in', no pressure, each message stands alone. List what I need to supply for each (the insight, the resource).
review: You confirm each follow-up delivers real value and that stop rules are set before you start.
metrics: Meetings booked from follow-ups versus first touch
risks: Sending to people who asked you to stop

name: Reply triage and qualification
goal: Sort replies quickly, draft careful responses, and keep the CRM accurate.
when: Daily, for every reply you receive.
inputs: The original message and account brief

steps.do: Paste the reply with the original message. Run the triage prompt to classify and draft a response.
Check the classification. Positive and sensitive replies are always answered by you personally.
Send your edited response. Honour opt-outs immediately.
Update status, next step and a one-line note. Add the contact to the suppression list if they opted out.

prompt:
Classify this reply and draft a response.

Original message:
[paste]

Reply:
[paste]

Classify as one of: interested, not now, wrong person, objection, unsubscribe, out-of-office, unclear.
Then:
1. Give your reasoning in one sentence.
2. Draft a response under 80 words (for 'unsubscribe', only confirm removal).
3. Suggest a CRM note (one line) and next step.
4. Flag anything I should handle personally (complaint, legal wording, pricing question).
Do not make claims about my product that I have not given you.
review: You handle every interested, sensitive or unclear reply yourself. Claude drafts and classifies only.
stop: Any unsubscribe or complaint: stop and suppress
Legal or compliance wording: escalate to a person
metrics: % of replies classified correctly on your spot check
